column2: THE DIRECTOR-GENERAL AND THE STAFF OF THE COMMISSION
(1) The Commission shall, in consultation with and

column1: with the approval of the President, appoint a suitable person,
possessing such qualifications and experience and local or
international  exposure  to  be  the  Director-General  of  the
Commission  (in  this  Act  referred  to  as  the  “Director-
General”).

column2: (2)  The  Director-General  shall  be  the  Chief  Executive

column1: Officer of the Commission.

column2: (3) The Director-General shall be appointed for a term of

column1: three years from the date of appointment on such terms and
conditions  as  may  be  determined  by  the  Commission  in
consultation  with  and  with  the  approval  of  the  President.
The  Director-General  shall  be  eligible  for  reappointment
unless removed from office in terms of subsection (6) of this
section.

column2: (4)  The  Director-General  shall,  subject  to  the  general

column1: direction and control of the Commission, be responsible for
the conduct of all affairs of the Commission.

column2: (5) The Director-General shall be paid such remuneration

column1: as may be determined by the Commission, in consultation
with the President.

column2: (6) The Commission may, in consultation with and with

column1: the approval of the President, for reasons assigned, remove
the Director-General from office.

column2: (7) The Director-General may resign from his office by a

column1: written  communication  in  that  regard  addressed  to  the
Commission and to the President, and such resignation shall
take effect on it being accepted by the President.
